chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Hamza ibn Humran, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I entered the market intending to buy a slave girl, and she said to me,
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying a slave girl who claims to be free?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the legal principle of 'istishab al-asl' (presumption of continuity) in the context of manumission, where the default state of a slave girl is slavery unless she produces definitive proof (bayyinah) of her freedom. It reflects the Shia juristic approach to commercial transactions, prioritizing the established status quo to prevent unjust loss of property rights for the buyer. The ruling underscores the evidentiary burden placed on the claimant of freedom, aligning with broader Islamic legal methodologies regarding ownership and emancipation.
